lessons.title: Start with the task
paragraphs: Begin with the thing someone came to do. Put the next useful action near the information it depends on, so the page does not make people search for a way forward.
A task list needs clear titles and useful status. An order review needs quantities and a total. A lesson needs readable content and a next step. Let those needs decide the layout.

lessons.title: Choose one primary action
paragraphs: Give the next step one consistent visual treatment. A filled button can mark that action while a quieter outlined control handles a secondary choice.
Keep the labels specific. Create task, save delivery, and continue lesson explain what will happen. Two equally strong actions can make the choice harder to read.

lessons.title: Use color with a purpose
paragraphs: A white page can still have a distinctive palette. Choose a deep action color, readable neutral text, and quiet separators. Apply the same roles consistently rather than introducing a new color for each section.
Keep state legible in words and shape as well as color. A checkmark and a Completed label say more than a green dot by itself. Make keyboard focus visible on every control.
